Lands the carry-out that a skill hands Claude one exact recipe, not editorial judgment — and outside that recipe, Claude has nothing written down to follow.

beats.narration_text: Here's the assumption to test. Claude already knows what belongs in a good funding digest. It doesn't — no model does. It has to be told, in a file it reads before acting. Here's what that file actually spells out.

Writer types the newcomer's wrong-guess word 'KNOWS' (implying Claude already possesses editorial judgment about what belongs in a digest), hesitates, corrects to 'has to be told' -> lands 'Claude already has to be told what a good funding digest should say, right?'. The wrong guess is picked up directly by B01's 'file it reads before acting' framing. Narration is >=30 words + lead_silence_s 0.8, giving the typing a >=9s window (TIMING LAW).

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening. A skill is a folder Claude reads before it does anything. This one is funding-digest. Inside sits SKILL.md — the full instruction set in plain English, no hidden logic, no compiled binary. Claude opens it, reads it, then acts. The file is the program.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline itself lives in the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it. Linear — top to bottom, no branching unless a step tells it to branch. Nothing else steers the run.

Here's the design choice, in both directions. Ask for exactly what the file names — a funding digest for the sectors or companies you're watching — and you get the same one-page slide, the same fields, every run. Ask for anything the file never mentions — a different format, a metric it doesn't list — and there's nothing behind it. They optimized for one recipe delivered exactly; they gave up flexibility to get it. The file is the entire spec.

shot.new_visual_element: Two columns: what the file names, what it never mentions — no verdict frame, per-item facts only

props.sparkLine: Named triggers get the same slide. Anything else has no spec to follow.
leftItems: deal flow digest, weekly recap, capital markets update — the exact trigger phrases
links back to the source deals in Capital IQ
rightItems: what happens if there's no new activity in your watched sector that week
no other output format is named — no doc, no multi-slide deck
no freshness window for "recent" is defined
any request outside those trigger phrases has nothing to fall back on

beats.narration_text: That's the carry-out. A skill doesn't make Claude judge what's newsworthy — it never did. It hands Claude one exact recipe. Outside that recipe, Claude has nothing written down to follow, and the model's guessing is not the same thing as your editorial judgment.

props.quote: A skill doesn't make Claude judge what's newsworthy. It gives Claude one exact recipe — and outside that recipe, Claude has nothing written down to follow.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Pick a report you regularly ask for — a weekly deal-flow digest, a status recap, anything you repeat. Then draft a one-page SKILL.md for it: name it, describe it in one line, list the exact steps to produce the output, and end by naming three things the skill would NOT cover. Go deeper: for one of those three, ask whether adding it belongs in this skill or in a separate one — and why.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to design a skill for a report I regularly ask for. Pick this report to work with: [name the report — e.g. a weekly deal-flow digest for the sectors I watch]. First, list every trigger phrase I'd say to invoke it, and every field the output should always contain. Then draft a one-page SKILL.md that Claude could read before acting: name the skill, describe what it does in one line, list the exact steps to produce the output, and note the specific inputs and output format it expects. End by naming three plausible requests a user might make that this skill would NOT cover — so I know exactly where the spec ends.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: for one of the three things your SKILL.md doesn't cover, ask whether adding it belongs in this skill or in a separate one — and why. That question is the difference between a skill that stays tight and a skill that quietly stops being reliable.
